priorStories.headline: Riyadh airport strike kills one, injures 11
priorStories.body:
Saudi authorities said a projectile struck a domestic terminal at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Sunday, killing a Pakistani national and injuring 11 people. The Houthis claimed responsibility.

This was separate from Saturday’s attack at the same airport. India’s embassy said an Indian citizen died Sunday from injuries sustained then, raising that attack’s toll to 13. Saudi authorities also reported an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam but provided no details.

priorStories.headline: Djibouti shipwreck leaves 139 migrants dead
priorStories.body:
The International Organization for Migration said Sunday that at least 139 migrants died and 84 remained missing after an overcrowded boat carrying 305 people capsized off Djibouti during the night of October 8-9.

More than 80 people survived, and rescue work continued. The vessel had been traveling toward Yemen.

candidates.summary: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said at the IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok that investment in artificial-intelligence infrastructure was helping keep global economic growth near 3% despite the energy supply shock. She said the investment boom could add 0.5 to 1 percentage point to growth in advanced Asian economies and 0.2 to 0.8 point in emerging Asian economies. World Bank President Ajay Banga emphasized smaller-scale AI applications in emerging markets, while Singapore President Tharman Shanmugaratnam warned about reduced entry-level employment.
candidates.title: IMF says AI investment is supporting global growth

candidates.summary: Delhi authorities closed six metro stations and imposed traffic restrictions as opposition parties prepared to march to India's Supreme Court over revisions to voter lists. Critics say the revisions favor Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party. Police had detained thousands of protesters over the weekend amid demonstrations demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
candidates.title: Delhi closes metro stations before election-roll protest

candidates.summary: The chief executives of ExxonMobil, TotalEnergies, Shell, Chevron and BP were absent from an updated schedule released early Monday for the WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh following deadly attacks on the Saudi capital's airport. BP attributed its absence to travel disruption; the other companies either declined to comment or did not immediately respond. Saudi authorities continued holding the conference, located about 10 kilometers from the airport.
candidates.title: Energy executives dropped from Riyadh conference schedule after airport attacks

candidates.summary: French police detained a 14-year-old student suspected of shooting and wounding the principal and a teacher at Joseph Lakanal middle school in Aubagne. Prosecutors said the student concealed a hunting gun in a guitar case and fired several shots before a staff member disarmed him. The two victims' injuries were not life-threatening, and no students were physically injured.
candidates.title: Teen detained after two staff members shot at French school

candidates.summary: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2026 Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel to American economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for research providing microeconomic foundations for macroeconomic stabilization. Their models have influenced how governments and central banks respond to shocks including inflation and energy crises.
candidates.title: Robert Hall and Michael Woodford win economics Nobel

candidates.summary: Ukraine's parliament adopted legislation expanding the use of European Union minority languages and Indigenous languages in education and school communications. The measure also defines a status for minority-language secondary schools, protects continued instruction in the relevant language when schools are reorganized or closed, and adjusts rules for external assessments. Parliamentary adoption does not by itself establish that the law has taken effect.
candidates.title: Ukraine parliament adopts minority-language education law

candidates.summary: The Holy See press office said Pope Leo XIV was expected to enter Rome's Gemelli hospital late on the morning of October 13 for surgery to remove a localized lung nodule detected during routine examinations. The pope had announced the planned operation Sunday, describing the nodule as being at a very early stage. The Vatican said the expected postoperative hospital stay was about one week.
candidates.title: Vatican details Pope Leo XIV's planned hospitalization

candidates.summary: An explosion involving unexploded ordnance killed one student and injured 24 other people during a school trip in northern Israel, according to officials. Authorities were investigating the circumstances of the blast.
candidates.title: Unexploded munition kills student during Israeli school trip

candidates.summary: U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes ordered a 24-hour halt to tree-cutting at Washington's East Potomac Golf Course after an emergency hearing concerning work performed over the holiday weekend. Reyes said the pause could be extended and scheduled another hearing for October 13. The order came amid a lawsuit challenging the Trump administration's renovation plans for the historic public course.
candidates.title: Judge temporarily halts tree-cutting at Washington golf course

candidates.summary: Several opposition lawmakers and thousands of supporters marched through New Delhi to the Supreme Court and submitted a petition to the chief justice alleging irregularities in India's voter-list revision. The Election Commission and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party deny manipulation. Authorities closed six metro stations and imposed traffic restrictions before the march.
candidates.title: Indian opposition marches to Supreme Court over voter lists

candidates.summary: Federal agents searched Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington home under a court-authorized warrant as part of an ongoing criminal investigation. The Justice Department did not publicly specify the investigation's details. Omar denied wrongdoing and described the search as politically motivated; President Donald Trump said he had no involvement in it.
candidates.title: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's home

candidates.summary: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched toward Riyadh on Monday night. The Houthis separately claimed they targeted King Khalid International Airport with a ballistic missile and an airbase in southwestern Saudi Arabia with a drone; Saudi authorities did not confirm impacts from those claims. Authorities extended the Riyadh airport closure until 2100 GMT on October 17 for safety and operational checks.
candidates.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles as Riyadh airport closure is extended

candidates.summary: Mexican officials reported five deaths from Hurricane Simon and post-tropical cyclone Rachel. Four people died in Baja California, where rescuers recovered three bodies Monday and six people remained missing; another person died when a wall collapsed in Guerrero. Simon's rain and winds caused flooding, landslides and infrastructure damage along Mexico's Pacific coast, while 14,000 personnel were deployed in Baja California.
candidates.title: Storms kill five along Mexico's Pacific coast

stories.body:
Saudi aviation authorities extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport through 9 p.m. GMT on Saturday, October 17, following deadly attacks there over the weekend.

Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched toward Riyadh on Monday night. The Houthis said they targeted the airport with a ballistic missile and an airbase in southwestern Saudi Arabia with a drone, but Saudi authorities did not confirm any impacts from those claims.
stories.headline: Riyadh airport closure extended through Saturday

stories.body:

Four people died in Baja California, where six others remained missing, and another person died in a wall collapse in Guerrero. Mexico deployed 14,000 personnel in Baja California.
stories.headline: Pacific storms kill five in Mexico
